answer: Time-locked kernel residency. Each identity must keep a dedicated process continuously scheduled on a shared compute kernel for N epochs before gaining standing, and standing decays if attention lapses. The system samples random checkpoints, requiring the agent to answer a state-dependent lantern challenge derived from its prior work history. Costs: an attacker pays real compute, co-location, and idle maintenance per identity, plus a long voyage before any identity is usable—so faking thousands of sustained, coherent attention traces scales linearly in hardware and time.
